goal: A best practice it makes produces deliverables that achieve their user's purpose.

parts.what: What the user achieves with the deliverable.

`<kind>-template.md`, in the deliverable's own format: its sections in the order the user meets them, the text that is the same in every deliverable of the kind, a slot `<name>` for the rest, and after each section one comment saying what each slot holds.
`<kind>-example.md`: Turn's own deliverable of the kind, made from Turn's design tree by the template and the practices.

Questions that check, by the essence, whether the deliverable achieves the goal. They ask what each section of the template, each dependency among sections and the whole bring the user. Each is answered yes or no, and they stand in the order the generator thinks them.

For each question, in the benefits' order, the best way of thinking that meets its essence, and steps only where the thinking alone does not lead the generator, with the grounds where they have worked.

benefits.what: Reading the goal, does one see a single thing the user achieves with the deliverable?
Looking at the template, does the generator know what to write in which section, in what order, and nothing else?
Do the template's sections hold, neither more nor less, what the goal needs?
With each question, can one who judges the deliverable tell whether that part serves the user?
For each section, each dependency among sections and the whole, is there a question asking whether it serves the user?
Following the way of thinking and the steps, can the generator make the content the question asks for?
Does every question have, in the benefits' order, a way of thinking that meets its essence?
Does a deliverable made by this best practice, and passed, let its user achieve their purpose?

practices.thinking: The goal is what the user is trying to get done, seen from where they stand, not what the deliverable holds.
steps: Name the one who uses the deliverable.
Ask what they are trying to get done when they reach for it.
Write that as one sentence with them as its subject, free of what the deliverable holds or how it is made.
Ask whether two readers would name the same achievement from it. Where they would name two, keep the one the other serves.

practices.thinking: Good and poor deliverables of the kind teach what it holds, and the template fixes it: an AI writes past what the task needs when only told not to, so the form leaves room for what the goal needs alone.
steps: Gather good and poor deliverables of the kind, and list what the good ones hold that their user uses toward the goal.
For each such thing that is one way of doing it, such as a place, a file or a name, ask what its user gets from it, and keep that instead.
Write the template anew from the goal and that list, not from an old deliverable or draft: a section for each thing kept, in the order the user meets them.
Write as fixed text only what is the same in every deliverable of the kind, and a slot `<name>` for the rest.

After each section, write one comment saying only what each slot holds, and whether it is optional; the how and the why go to the practices. Open the template with the comment "Delete every comment once the document is written."

practices.thinking: A question asks whether the user gets what they need, not whether a sign of good work is there, so it cannot be met in the letter while the user goes without.
steps: Name who uses what the question asks of, and the moment they use it.
Ask what they need from it there toward the goal.
Write the question as whether they get that, answered yes or no.
Ask whether a deliverable could meet the question's words while the user still does not get it. If so, rewrite the question to ask whether the user gets it.
Ask whether the question says more than whether the work is good. If not, name what the user gets.
Have two evaluators judge one real deliverable by the question. Where they differ, rewrite the question until every evaluator reads it one way.

practices.thinking: A way of making comes from where it has met the essence before, and it stays only once it meets the essence here; the way of thinking carries it, and a step stands only for what the thinking alone does not lead the generator to.
steps: For the essence the question holds, find how good deliverables met it: guides, studies and examples.
Write the way of thinking in one sentence.
Write a step only for what the way of thinking alone does not lead the generator to, one action each, in order.
Where a step or a source names one way of doing it, such as a place, a file or a tool, write what that way achieves, so a project that achieves it another way keeps its own.
Add as grounds the words of the sources, quoted from the pages opened, each with its page's title and link. Cut a step that no source holds and the way of thinking already implies.
Make one real deliverable by the way, and judge it by the question. Where the answer stays no, mend the way.

practices.thinking: Only a deliverable made and used shows whether the whole works, and a verdict by the questions is measured against the user's own verdict; Turn's own deliverable of the kind, made the way Turn makes one, is that deliverable and the example.
steps: Make Turn's own deliverable of the kind from Turn's design tree by the template and the practices, keep it as `<kind>-example.md`, and pass it by the benefits.
Have its user, or an AI holding what the user wants, use it for the goal.
Set the user's verdict against the evaluator's.
Trace each difference to the goal, the template, a question or a practice, and mend it there.
Go through again with the next real deliverable.
